jp-west-p1-iij-matsue-power-agreement-20.summary: IIJ's release of 5 October 2026 announces that IIJ concluded, that day, a disaster power-supply agreement with Matsue City. Under it IIJ will use the large-capacity lithium-ion batteries and EV chargers installed at its IIJ Matsue Data Center Park (Matsue DCP) to supply two municipal community centres used as evacuation shelters, reserving about 1,000 kWh for the city. The release states that the installed batteries are operated as backup power for the data-centre facilities and are used for the shelters in a disaster, and that in normal times they also support local demand-response requests. It describes the existing Matsue DCP; it gives no new building, phase, capacity, construction, pause or closure.
jp-west-p1-iij-matsue-power-agreement-20.title: IIJ concludes disaster power-supply agreement with Matsue City using the batteries installed at the IIJ Matsue Data Center Park (press release, 5 October 2026)

us-south-central-p1-enid-project-thunder.summary: Plainsmen Holdings, LLC announced plans to develop Project Thunderbird, 'a data center and power corridor infrastructure initiative' in Enid and Garfield County. The proposed development encompasses approximately 1,735 acres across four campuses in Enid and includes plans for an on-site power generation facility of up to 3.3 gigawatts through a partnership with an unnamed natural gas midstream provider; the project would use raw water from the Kaw Lake Pipeline and closed-loop cooling. A related Patriot Utility District would provide backup power and fiber for Vance Air Force Base. The release says further details will be announced; it names no campus tract, IT capacity, operator or schedule.

status_updates.identity_review: The release names IIJ松江データセンターパーク (Matsue DCP), IIJ's own campus in Matsue, Shimane, which is the existing site IIJ Matsue Data Center Park and its single project IIJ Matsue Existing Operations (owner and operator Internet Initiative Japan; identity pages iij.ad.jp/biz/dc/matsue.html and iij.ad.jp/datacenter/tech/iijdc/matsuedcp.html already attached). The release names no other IIJ facility in Matsue. The batteries and EV chargers are equipment installed at that campus, not a separate facility, so the refresh keeps the whole-campus scope and the reviewed campus locator unchanged. Checked against the current dataset (2026-10-22-research-fortyfirst): the only Atlas record within 2 km of the campus point is the site itself; the nearest other site is Enecom Hiroshima Data Center, 132.9 km away. No pending queue fragment or hold concerns Matsue.

status.summary: In its release of 5 October 2026 IIJ states that the large-capacity lithium-ion batteries installed at its IIJ Matsue Data Center Park are operated as backup power for the data-centre facilities, and commits about 1,000 kWh of that stored power to Matsue City's evacuation shelters under a disaster power-supply agreement concluded that day. This is the operator's present-tense description of the existing campus in service on 5 October 2026. It establishes no new building, phase, capacity, utilisation or construction; the planned disaster drills are future work.
